requested_checks.question: For backend during 2026-10-01T11:45:00Z-2026-10-01T13:00:00Z, discover the actual available metric names and report connection-pool (active, max, waiters), cpu_utilization, memory_utilization, request latency, and error rate series to distinguish pool misconfiguration from local resource saturation.
requested_checks.reason: Empty metric_names first surfaces the real metric set so pool and resource series can be compared on the same timeline before any root-cause claim.
requested_checks.expected_discriminator: Pool waiters elevated with flat cpu/memory and pool_active at max indicates pool misconfiguration; rising cpu/memory together with latency indicates local resource saturation.

requested_checks.question: During 2026-10-01T11:45:00Z-2026-10-01T13:00:00Z, do postgres show connection exhaustion, lock waits, or slow queries that could back-pressure backend pool waiters?
requested_checks.reason: Backend pool waiters could be driven by a downstream postgres bottleneck; database telemetry discriminates whether postgres is the pressure source.
requested_checks.expected_discriminator: Active sessions near the connection limit, non-zero lock waits, or slow queries indicate postgres pressure; absent these, the pool bottleneck is local to backend configuration.
